Headroom on the minimum runway covenant narrowed from {{fact:406c40a8-c588-4040-af98-afe0429ccf53}} to {{fact:05172343-e33a-447f-929b-b97a25beb1f4}} to {{fact:d17b43e9-1b63-4865-9051-65f587a66bce}}. The breach looks real. Revenue to Plan (Section 6.3) for the three months ended October 31, 2026 came to {{fact:2aa946f7-88cb-43f5-9d81-36858ba826b6}}. The minimum is {{fact:86b794ce-e84e-4abc-994a-281808cbcc21}}, so the shortfall is {{fact:6571fa4a-90b8-4cb3-b718-3e9e95db9631}}. The borrower's own October certificate agrees: it reports {{fact:194229d5-2cee-41c8-a7b3-fc68f0dd8337}} and says the borrower was not in compliance. The test has no add-backs, so no add-back cap can explain it. Only one terms version is on file (version 1, approved, from the original agreement). No unapproved amendments are on file. A search of the documents found no waiver and no written update to the Approved Plan. Rerunning the test under version 1 gave the same failure. The September certificate also reports the borrower out of compliance with this covenant, so the shortfall is not limited to one month. How the bank responds is for the credit team to decide.

Revenue against plan stands at {{fact:d3c0308e-5362-4a2d-add5-7f48ba7438ce}}, below the covenant level of {{fact:2b1e9f12-88af-480c-8839-8321fdd53587}}, so headroom is negative at {{fact:143008c9-152b-4303-8b94-f0ec44e56200}}. The test is not merely tight but already on the wrong side of the threshold. The revenue shortfall and trend signals describe the same problem.

Revenue came in at only {{fact:7c03c73e-aea4-4930-a6c3-32d6151c4c01}} of plan, a substantial miss for a subscription business that usually plans revenue with some visibility. This shortfall is what drives the failed revenue covenant and may also explain the steady erosion in cash headroom.

Headroom on the revenue covenant has worsened each month, from {{fact:bd640ec7-ecf0-43d3-a63d-9192b211663f}} in August to {{fact:a542ff08-ffd1-4346-a466-7861b003c49b}} in September and {{fact:143008c9-152b-4303-8b94-f0ec44e56200}} in October. The miss is deepening rather than a one-off, which makes the current shortfall harder to dismiss as timing.

Unrestricted cash of {{fact:dbd79489-2b03-4727-a834-ad64cbe6d2f4}} is still well above the {{fact:470a0286-54f6-4cc7-9317-4263d93d03ed}} minimum, but headroom has slid from {{fact:fdb0de1b-4a3b-4926-a56f-074e66e78c2b}} in August to {{fact:646000c5-6cea-46af-87a0-9d19e4f548b5}} in October. Falling cash alongside a widening revenue miss may point to burn that the business is not covering with sales.

Dataflake has about {{fact:78f6ae81-0bfe-4964-bff9-c570772de4ee}} months of cash at current burn, which limits its ability to absorb setbacks before it needs new funding. The low-severity runway covenant signal shows this has been shrinking quickly. The cash covenant signals show the same pressure on its balance sheet.

Unrestricted cash of {{fact:c6b23fca-d829-47de-afb9-2c23d0a23106}} is below the {{fact:dfe07fca-0fbc-40ee-b40b-3a228a34e2f2}} minimum, giving headroom of {{fact:4485e2b5-96b8-4ad6-ba54-6343194e8b1c}}. This is the trend behind the high-severity runway signal.

Cash covenant headroom moved from {{fact:c62ed519-9cd5-4290-86ff-3a880e7c459e}} in August to {{fact:34304bd5-0c7c-4ff3-a214-d8e31aa6b48b}} in September, then to {{fact:4485e2b5-96b8-4ad6-ba54-6343194e8b1c}} in October.
